## 1 — Setup (once per computer)

**Install:**

- **VS Code** — [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com) (tick **"Add to PATH"** during setup)
- **Quarto CLI** — [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/)
- **Quarto extension** for VS Code — search "Quarto" in the Extensions sidebar

**Create the project:**

**File → New File… → Quarto Project → Website Project** → choose your folder. Quarto creates:

- `_quarto.yml` — project-wide settings (see page 2)
- `index.qmd` — your homepage
- `about.qmd` — an example second page
- `styles.css` — optional custom styling

Ready to start editing? See **Preview vs. Render** at the end of page 2 before you do.

```{=latex}

```

## 2 — Writing & editing content

Every `.qmd` file is a **YAML header** followed by a **Markdown body**. There are two separate, independent levels of YAML — don't confuse them:

1. **Project-wide, one file:** `_quarto.yml` sets navigation, theme, and defaults for the *entire* site. It exists once per project — you only touch it for site-wide changes, not for every page.
2. **Per page, every file:** the `---`-fenced header at the *top of each* `.qmd` file. Every page has one; it sets that page's own title and can override the project's defaults just for itself.

Project-wide (`_quarto.yml`):

```yaml
website:
  title: "My Site"
  navbar:
    left:
      - text: "About"
        href: about.qmd
```

Per page (top of `my-page.qmd`):

```yaml
---
title: "My Page"
format: html
filters:
  - parmsam/quizdown
---
```

**Markdown body basics:**

| Syntax | Result |
|---|---|
| `## Heading` | Section heading |
| `**bold**`, `*italic*` | **bold**, *italic* |
| `` `code` `` | inline code |
| `- item` / `1. item` | Bulleted / numbered list |
| `> text` | Blockquote |
| `[text](url)` | Link |
| `![](path.png)` | Image |
| `$x^2$`, `$$x^2$$` | Inline / block math |
| fence tagged `{python}` | Executable code cell (see below) |
| `::: {.callout-tip} ... :::` | Callout box |

**Callouts** flag information visually:

```markdown
::: {.callout-tip}
## Tip
Use tips for best-practice advice.
:::
```

renders as:

::: {.callout-tip}
## Tip
Use tips for best-practice advice.
:::

Other types: `.callout-note`, `.callout-warning`, `.callout-important`.

**Code cells:** open a fence tagged `{python}` (or `{pyodide-python}` for interactive) and close it with a plain fence, e.g.:

```python
#| echo: false   # hide the code, keep the output
#| eval: true    # run the cell (default)
print("Hello!")
```

Common cell options (as `#|` comments): `echo`, `eval`, `warning`, `error`, `output`.

**Preview vs. Render:**

| Command | What it does | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| **Preview** button, or `quarto preview` | Opens a live local view; updates automatically every time you save a file | While you're writing and editing |
| `quarto render` | Builds the final static output files into `_site` (or `docs/`, if configured) — no live view opens | Before publishing, or to produce the files to upload |

::: {.callout-note}
## Tip
The **Preview** button does both at once: it renders your site and opens the live view. You only need a separate `quarto render` when you want the output files *without* opening a preview — e.g. right before publishing.
:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

## 3 — Publish with GitHub Pages

1. In `_quarto.yml`, under `project:`, add `output-dir: docs`
2. Render: `quarto render`
3. Create a **public** repository on [github.com](https://github.com)
4. Upload the whole project folder (including `docs/`) and commit
5. Repo → **Settings → Pages** → Branch `main`, folder `/docs` → **Save**
6. Wait for the green checkmark under **Deployments** — your site is live at
   `https://<username>.github.io/<repo-name>/`

**Updating your site later:** run `quarto render` again, then re-upload the `docs/` folder to GitHub (or `git push` if you're using Git).

```{=latex}
\begin{spotlight}{Good to know}
\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{site-url:} in \texttt{\_quarto.yml} sets the canonical base URL --- needed for correct social-share previews and RSS links.
\item \texttt{repo-url:} and \texttt{page-footer:} add an automatic ``Edit this page'' / source-code link and a custom footer, site-wide.
\item Renaming or moving a \texttt{.qmd} file changes its output URL. Plan file names before publishing --- old links to a renamed page will 404.
\end{itemize}
\end{spotlight}
```
